title: Representation Learning of Temporal Graphs with Structural Roles

problem.claim: Temporal graph representation learning must model both local dependencies and global structural role information.

gap.claim: Existing methods mainly model local structural dependencies and therefore underestimate global structural roles.

contributions.claim: RTGCN is a temporal graph convolution network that leverages global structural role information.
RTGCN captures static global structural roles with hypergraph convolution and role evolution with structural role-based gated recurrent units.
RTGCN incorporates structural role proximity into its objective to preserve global structural similarity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe RTGCN as a novel approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On multiple real-world datasets, RTGCN reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art temporal graph representation learning methods across temporal link prediction and node classification tasks.
The authors report up to 5.1% AUC improvement for link prediction and up to 6.2% F1 improvement for new link prediction.
The authors report up to 4.6% AUC improvement for node classification and 2.7% improvement for structural role classification.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal graph representation learning has received substantial attention.
Existing work emphasizes local dependencies while underestimating global structural roles.
RTGCN models static roles, evolving roles, and global role similarity through three integrated components.
Experiments reportedly show improvements across several temporal graph prediction and classification tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets or baseline methods.
